routes.name: Atom
routes.configuration: Atom full BASIC configuration
routes.input_contract: INPUT A replaces the numeric A after Return; only 1 is an action in the caller. The input routine preserves N.
routes.audio_contract: The FOR loop toggles PPI port C bit 2 at #B002. This is a blocking software tone; J is scratch state. Other port-C bits are read and written back. Competing writers still need coordination.
routes.custom_input: Use another number for a different command, or add a separate test after the reader. INPUT also accepts values the game does not recognise.
routes.custom_audio: Change the iteration count for a longer burst. Its pitch and length depend on interpreter/CPU execution; a tone generator or interrupt driver is a different component.
routes.references: Acorn, Atom BASIC Manual: INPUT, GOSUB/RETURN, byte indirection and bitwise operators; Atom Technical Manual: 8255 port C and loudspeaker.

routes.name: Amstrad CPC
routes.configuration: CPC464 PAL, Locomotive BASIC, MODE 1
routes.input_contract: INPUT A$ waits for a complete line. The caller compares A$ with the exact uppercase string GO; reading a line does not validate it.
routes.audio_contract: SOUND 1,100,10,15 submits a channel-A note to the firmware sound system. This routine returns after submission, subject to the firmware queue being able to accept the command. Firmware owns subsequent playback.
routes.custom_input: Replace GO with a short command or dispatch several strings after the reader. Keep the line-number range free.
routes.custom_audio: Change the SOUND period, duration or volume operands. Adding envelopes changes the duration contract; filling the firmware queue can make submission wait.
routes.references: Amstrad, CPC464 User Instructions: Locomotive BASIC entries INPUT, GOSUB, RETURN and SOUND, including channel/queue behaviour.

routes.name: Atari 800XL
routes.configuration: 800XL NTSC, Atari BASIC and GRAPHICS 0
routes.input_contract: INPUT A replaces one numeric variable; the caller accepts 1 and rejects 0. It does not poll a joystick or run while the player edits a line.
routes.audio_contract: SOUND channel 0 is started with frequency 100, distortion 10 and volume 15; a BASIC loop delays before SOUND 0,0,0,0 mutes it. J is scratch.
routes.custom_input: Validate the submitted value before moving a piece or changing a room. Keep game state out of the reader.
routes.custom_audio: Choose another frequency/distortion pair. The FOR loop is a blocking CPU delay; it is not a calibrated wall clock or a POKEY music sequencer.
routes.references: Atari, Atari BASIC Reference Manual: INPUT, GOSUB/RETURN and SOUND; Atari Hardware Manual: POKEY audio channels.

routes.name: Commodore PET
routes.configuration: 40-column PET firmware configuration with emulated VIA/CB2 sound output
routes.input_contract: INPUT A$ returns a whole line; the caller recognises GO. N survives the subroutine. The ROM owns keyboard scanning and its editing buffer.
routes.audio_contract: The routine programs VIA ACR, shift register and Timer 2 low byte at 59467, 59466 and 59464, waits in a BASIC loop, then clears ACR. It requires an audible CB2 sound connection or the selected emulator output; an early PET without a speaker connection is not magically given a speaker.
routes.custom_input: Use another string or add a dispatch table after INPUT. Changing case handling is a separate decision.
routes.custom_audio: Change the Timer 2 operand to alter the output. This takes over VIA shift-register/timer configuration; it does not preserve another driver or restore a previous ACR value.
routes.references: Commodore, PET/CBM documentation: BASIC INPUT and GOSUB/RETURN; MOS Technology 6522 VIA data sheet: ACR, shift-register modes and Timer 2; PET sound requires the appropriate CB2 connection.

routes.name: Commodore VIC-20
routes.configuration: unexpanded PAL VIC-20, Commodore BASIC
routes.input_contract: INPUT A$ returns a submitted line. The example accepts GO; held-key repeat during editing belongs to the ROM, not to game turns.
routes.audio_contract: POKE 36878,15 changes shared master volume; POKE 36876,220 enables the third tone voice. After a blocking J loop, POKE 36876,0 stops that voice.
routes.custom_input: Add another string-to-action branch. Do not assume a string returned by INPUT is already a valid game command.
routes.custom_audio: Change the voice register value for another tone. Preserve or explicitly own master volume when mixing effects and music; this sample leaves volume at 15.
routes.references: Commodore, VIC-20 Programmer’s Reference Guide: BASIC INPUT/GOSUB and VIC sound registers $900A–$900E.

routes.name: Dragon 32
routes.configuration: Dragon 32 PAL, stock Extended Colour BASIC
routes.input_contract: INPUT A waits for a submitted number; the caller accepts 1. The routine reads a value and leaves the decision to its caller.
routes.audio_contract: SOUND 100,2 uses the ROM sound routine and blocks while it generates the tone. Those operands are BASIC pitch/duration units, not frequency and seconds.
routes.custom_input: Choose another accepted number or dispatch several numeric commands. INPUT is useful when the world can wait.
routes.custom_audio: Change the SOUND operands using the language manual’s ranges. A non-blocking player would need to take over the audio path and its timing.
routes.references: Dragon Data, Dragon 32 User Manual: INPUT, GOSUB/RETURN and SOUND; ROM sound generation.

routes.name: Mattel Aquarius
routes.configuration: stock Aquarius BASIC with an array-backed USR sound helper
routes.input_contract: GOSUB 4000 replaces A$ with the submitted line. The caller recognises GO. The 4000 range deliberately leaves the existing 3000-range sound DATA intact.
routes.audio_contract: The caller creates all its scalar variables before DIM Z(16), locates that array storage and installs a 22-byte Z80 helper plus USR vector. GOSUB 2000 calls it. It toggles output port $FC with a CPU delay and returns, preserving AF/BC. The routine blocks and uses W/J/B/X plus the Z array and USR vector.
routes.custom_input: Reserve the complete numbered ranges. Reusing line 3000 for INPUT replaces a sound DATA line; the native fault run fails before the game starts. The repaired program uses 4000/4010.
routes.custom_audio: Keep the array/vector setup with the sound routine. Adding variables or changing array layout can move its storage; do not reuse a stale pointer. A ROM-independent allocator/driver would need a different storage contract.
routes.references: Mattel/Radofin, Aquarius BASIC documentation: INPUT, DATA/READ, DIM and USR; machine-code helper bytes and port behaviour are identified by this configuration’s executed source.

routes.name: MSX1
routes.configuration: MSX1 NTSC, recorded MSX BASIC/BIOS
routes.input_contract: INPUT A$ waits for a line and replaces A$. GO is accepted by the caller. The test’s byte at 40000 mirrors the game count; it is not the input routine’s output.
routes.audio_contract: BASIC SOUND writes start PSG tone A using period 100 and mixer operand 62, set volume 15, delay with J, then mute volume A. The routine blocks. Leave firmware/PSG port-direction handling to BASIC; do not transplant the mixer operand as an uncontrolled hardware write.
routes.custom_input: Use a different command string or connect the reader to a parser. The separate assembly loop shows physical press edges.
routes.custom_audio: Change the tone period or volume; choose a serviced player when animation/music must continue. The caller lowers BASIC’s allocation ceiling below its diagnostic byte at 40000.
routes.references: ASCII/Microsoft, MSX Technical Data Book: BASIC INPUT, CLEAR, SOUND, GOSUB/RETURN; PSG and BIOS ownership.

routes.name: Oric Atmos
routes.configuration: Oric Atmos, stock BASIC text mode
routes.input_contract: INPUT A waits for a numeric line. Only 1 advances the example; 0 is ignored. INPUT itself is not a one-key scanner.
routes.audio_contract: PING uses the firmware’s predefined effect. The wrapper has no custom state or parameters; its timing/control belongs to the ROM effect.
routes.custom_input: Replace the numeric test or dispatch several commands after the read. Use a character reader for a menu that should respond before Return.
routes.custom_audio: Use another documented ROM effect or write an AY routine with an explicit mixer/channel contract. PING is deliberately a small interface, not an arbitrary note player.
routes.references: Oric, Atmos Manual: BASIC INPUT, GOSUB/RETURN and PING; predefined sound effects.

routes.name: Spectravideo SVI-328
routes.configuration: SVI-328 NTSC, stock BASIC
routes.input_contract: INPUT A$ returns a line. The caller accepts GO and stores its byte count above BASIC’s lowered allocation ceiling. The mirror is diagnostic state, not an input API.
routes.audio_contract: SOUND starts PSG tone A, then a blocking J loop delays before muting it. The routine owns those tone/mixer/volume settings; it does not arbitrate with music.
routes.custom_input: Connect the returned string to a larger command dispatcher. Keep CLEAR’s reserved address and any machine-code or asset allocations consistent.
routes.custom_audio: Change the period or use another channel with an explicit mixer policy. Busy-loop duration depends on the interpreter and workload.
routes.references: Spectravideo, SVI BASIC documentation: CLEAR, INPUT, SOUND, GOSUB/RETURN and PSG sound control.

routes.name: Atari 2600
routes.configuration: NTSC 4 KiB cartridge
routes.input_contract: INPT4 at $0C uses active-low bit 7. The inline sampler normalises it to 0/$80 in A and current byte $84. It changes A and flags; X/Y are untouched.
routes.audio_contract: TIA channel 0 ($15/$17/$19), duration byte $85; trigger changes A/flags and service changes A/flags. The caller owns TIA/RIOT and the software scanline schedule.
routes.custom_input: Change the input mask only with the correct electrical source. Paddle inputs and a second fire arrangement need different readers.
routes.custom_audio: Change AUDC0/AUDF0/AUDV0 for another effect. Keep all work within the overscan budget; moving a blocking effect here can break the picture.
routes.references: Atari, Stella Programmer’s Guide: INPT4, VBLANK/WSYNC and audio registers; MOS 6507/RIOT execution.

routes.name: Atari 5200
routes.configuration: NTSC 32 KiB cartridge, recorded BIOS handover
routes.input_contract: GTIA TRIG0 at $C010 uses active-low bit 0. The inline sampler stores 0/1 in current=$1004, leaving the edge decision to its caller; A/flags change.
routes.audio_contract: POKEY channel 1 at $E800/$E801, duration byte $1005. The trigger also sets global AUDCTL and SKCTL; it is not isolated from other POKEY users. A/flags change.
routes.custom_input: This reads the fire trigger only. The 5200’s analogue axes require their own sampling/calibration policy.
routes.custom_audio: Change the frequency/distortion values after deciding who owns global POKEY configuration. A cartridge must retain the BIOS entry contract.
routes.references: Atari, 5200/GTIA hardware documentation: trigger inputs; POKEY data sheet: AUDF/AUDC/AUDCTL/SKCTL; ANTIC VCOUNT.

routes.name: Atari 7800
routes.configuration: NTSC 48 KiB cartridge, reset without BIOS authentication
routes.input_contract: Legacy INPT4 at $0C uses active-low bit 7; the inline sampler stores 0/$80 in current=$1904. It changes A/flags and does not read the second independent controller button.
routes.audio_contract: Stock TIA channel 0, duration byte $1905; no cartridge POKEY is assumed. A/flags change. The caller owns MARIA display lists, TIA sound and its mode lock.
routes.custom_input: Add the second controller button only after handling its distinct wiring. Do not copy the 5200 bit-0 trigger mask.
routes.custom_audio: Change TIA tone/noise controls; a POKEY cartridge is an expanded audio configuration with another implementation.
routes.references: Atari, 7800 Software Guide: controller/TIA interface, MARIA/MSTAT and cartridge reset; Stella audio register definitions.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$6001; turn=$6000, field clock=$6002/$6003; stack below $63F0
routes.name: ColecoVision
routes.configuration: NTSC ColecoVision, recorded BIOS, title-skipping cartridge
routes.input_contract: The caller selects joystick mode with OUT ($C0),A. IN ($FC) then reads controller 1: left fire is active-low bit 6. The inline sampler returns 0/$40 in B and changes A/flags/B.
routes.audio_contract: SN76489 tone 0 at port $FF, duration byte $6005. Trigger preserves AF and B; service changes AF. Picture initialisation mutes all channels, so the complete caller takes audio ownership.
routes.custom_input: Keep controller mode selection with the reader; keypad mode gives another meaning to the same read. Share mode changes explicitly.
routes.custom_audio: Change the PSG’s ten-bit tone divisor or attenuation. Latched register writes must remain ordered; concurrent sound writers need arbitration.
routes.references: Coleco, ColecoVision technical documentation: controller mode ports and cartridge vectors; Texas Instruments SN76489A data manual: latch/data writes.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$DF01; turn=$DF00, field clock=$DF02/$DF03; stack below $F7F0
routes.name: Memotech MTX
routes.configuration: MTX500 PAL, stock BASIC DATA/POKE/USR entry
routes.input_contract: OUT ($05),$7F selects keyboard column 7; IN ($06) supplies the high part of its return. Space is active-low bit 0 of that read. B receives 0/1; AF/B change.
routes.audio_contract: SN76489 tone 0 writes port $06, duration $DF05. Reads at $06 belong to keyboard input while writes belong to sound. Trigger preserves AF/B; service changes AF.
routes.custom_input: Preserve the read/write distinction and column drive. This direct reader takes over the keyboard configuration rather than consuming a BASIC character.
routes.custom_audio: Change the tone divisor or duration counter. The USR entry takes over until reset; it does not return to a live BASIC session.
routes.references: Memotech, MTX Series Operator’s Manual/technical description: keyboard matrix, sound I/O and USR; TI SN76489A data manual.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$C001; turn=$C000, field clock=$C002/$C003; SP=$FFFE, interrupts disabled
routes.name: Game Boy
routes.configuration: DMG default reset without boot ROM, 32 KiB cartridge
routes.input_contract: Writing $10 to JOYP selects action buttons. Six settling reads precede active-low bit-0 normalisation; B receives 0/1 for A. AF/B change, and the row remains selected.
routes.audio_contract: Pulse channel 1, duration byte $C004. The trigger also writes shared NR50/NR51/NR52 routing, volume and power controls, so it is not safe beside an unrelated mixer. AF changes; B is preserved.
routes.custom_input: Use another JOYP row or combine rows deliberately. Hardware switch bounce and input lost between polls are separate from the release/press filter.
routes.custom_audio: Change pulse duty/frequency/envelope operands. An audio engine should initialise shared power/routing once and arbitrate channel use.
routes.references: Nintendo, Game Boy Programming Manual v1.1: P1/JOYP scan example (six action-button reads), LCDC/LY access rules and NR10–NR14/NR50–NR52.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$C001; turn=$C000, field clock=$C002/$C003; stack below $C3F0
routes.name: Game Gear
routes.configuration: NTSC stock Game Gear cartridge configuration
routes.input_contract: IN ($DC) reads the pad. Active-low bit 4 is button 1; B receives 0/$10. AF/B change. START is not part of this sampler.
routes.audio_contract: SN76489-compatible tone 0 at $7F, duration $C005. Trigger preserves AF/B; service changes AF. No stereo-panning interface is provided here.
routes.custom_input: Add other pad bits after defining your game’s mask. START and stereo routing are Game Gear-specific extensions, not Master System aliases.
routes.custom_audio: Change the tone divisor or attenuation. A stereo effect needs a separate routing contract as well as a tone.
routes.references: Sega, Game Gear hardware/software reference: controller ports, stereo routing and PSG; TI SN76489A latch/data format.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$C001; turn=$C000, field clock=$C002/$C003; stack below $C3F0
routes.name: Master System
routes.configuration: NTSC stock Master System cartridge configuration
routes.input_contract: IN ($DC), complement and mask $10 returns button 1 as 0/$10 in B. AF/B change. The caller does not change pad I/O direction mid-read.
routes.audio_contract: PSG tone 0 at $7F, duration $C005; trigger preserves AF/B, service changes AF. FM audio is not part of this stock PSG routine.
routes.custom_input: Combine direction/button bits into one sample before calculating edges. Light guns and paddles need different readers.
routes.custom_audio: Change the tone divisor or duration. A music/effect priority policy can sit above this register writer.
routes.references: Sega, Master System Software Reference Manual: I/O port $DC, controller interface, VDP status and PSG.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$C001; turn=$C000, field clock=$C002/$C003; stack below $C3F0
routes.name: SG-1000
routes.configuration: NTSC stock SG-1000 cartridge configuration
routes.input_contract: Controller port $DC returns active-low button-1 bit 4. B receives 0/$10; AF/B change.
routes.audio_contract: SN76489 tone 0 at $7F, duration $C005; trigger preserves AF/B, service changes AF. The cartridge fits the base RAM configuration used here.
routes.custom_input: Keep pad sampling separate from display modes; shared pad/PSG ideas do not make the SG-1000 VDP a Master System VDP.
routes.custom_audio: Change divisor/attenuation with the same latch protocol. A full player needs independent channel state and an explicit work budget.
routes.references: Sega, SG-1000 technical documentation: controller/PSG I/O; TI SN76489A and TMS9918A data manuals.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$7001; turn=$7000, field clock=$7002/$7003; stack below $7FF0
routes.name: Sord M5
routes.configuration: NTSC M5, monitor-started cartridge
routes.input_contract: IN ($30) reads keyboard row Y0. Space is ACTIVE-HIGH bit 6: mask $40 and keep its polarity. B receives 0/$40; AF/B change.
routes.audio_contract: SN76489 tone 0 at $20, duration $7005. Trigger preserves AF/B; service changes AF. The caller owns the VDP and starts through the monitor cartridge header.
routes.custom_input: Do not add the complement used by neighbouring Z80 machines: an idle M5 would look pressed. Other keyboard rows need their own selection/read contract.
routes.custom_audio: Change the divisor or attenuation. Keep SN76489 writes separate from VDP status reads at $11; both chips need ownership, for different reasons.
routes.references: Sord BASIC-G Appendix H: I/O map; Sord M5C-01 schematic: decoding; TI SN76489A and TMS9918A data manuals. The specific Space polarity is configuration-specific executed evidence.

routes.memory_contract: previous=$8001; turn=$8000, field clock=$8002/$8003; stack below $FFF0
routes.name: Tatung Einstein
routes.configuration: TC-01 PAL, MOS 1.2, Ctrl-BREAK disk boot
routes.input_contract: Select AY register 14 and write $FE for keyboard row 0, then select register 15 and read port $02. Space is active-low bit 6. B receives 0/$40; AF/B and the AY register selection change.
routes.audio_contract: AY channel A, duration $8005. The routine sets mixer $7E, preserving the required port-A-output/port-B-input configuration. Trigger preserves AF/B; service changes AF. Both keyboard and sound share the AY address latch.
routes.custom_input: Keep the dedicated keyboard interrupt masked as in startup, or synchronise all AY register selections. An interrupt between address and data accesses can redirect a write.
routes.custom_audio: Change tone A’s period/volume without changing keyboard port directions. A shared audio driver must coordinate with keyboard scanning.
routes.references: Tatung, Einstein Hardware Manual: programmable sound generator/keyboard interface and port decoding; MOS disk boot header; General Instrument AY-3-8910 data manual.

routes.name: Jupiter Ace
routes.configuration: stock 3 KiB Ace, recorded FORTH ROM
routes.input_contract: NEWKEY has stack effect ( -- c ). It waits for INKEY to return zero, then waits for a nonzero character. A key held at entry must be released before it can become a new action. It preserves everything already below its result on the data stack.
routes.audio_contract: CLICK has stack effect ( -- ). It supplies 478 and 120 to ROM BEEP, which consumes both operands and blocks for the generated tone. The running turn count below them stays on the stack.
routes.custom_input: Change the character comparison after NEWKEY. Keep release-then-press when an action must happen once per physical press; raw INKEY is useful for held-state controls instead.
routes.custom_audio: Change CLICK’s two BEEP operands using the manual’s pitch/duration rules. Their units are not interchangeable with BASIC SOUND on other machines.
routes.references: Jupiter Cantab, Jupiter Ace User Manual: INKEY, ?DUP, conditional loops and BEEP; chapter on the loudspeaker and music.

routes.name: Sinclair ZX80
routes.configuration: stock 4 KiB ROM, 1 KiB RAM, keyword entry
routes.input_contract: INPUT A is a blocking numeric reader. The nine-line caller adds the submitted A to N; it is a running total, not a validator restricted to 0 and 1. Entering 2 adds two.
routes.audio_contract: The stock machine has no programmable speaker. No stock sound routine is supplied. An external sound interface would be a separate target configuration.
routes.custom_input: Copy the INPUT statement into your own numbered flow. Preserve N between decisions. At 1 KiB, the program and its display compete for memory.
routes.custom_audio: An expansion needs its own hardware contract and tests; a silent placeholder cannot stand in for an implemented audio route.
routes.references: Sinclair, ZX80 Operating Manual: INPUT, integer arithmetic, program/display memory and keyboard entry; stock ROM execution in the named 1 KiB configuration.

routes.name: Sinclair ZX81
routes.configuration: stock PAL ROM, 1 KiB RAM, keyword entry
routes.input_contract: INPUT A is a blocking numeric reader. The caller performs N=N+A, so any valid numeric contribution is added; 0 leaves the total alone. It is not a one-key accept/reject routine.
routes.audio_contract: The stock machine has no programmable speaker. Sound expansions need their own implementation and qualification.
routes.custom_input: Keep the normal display-serviced environment used here. FAST/SLOW choices change what the player sees while the CPU works; the sample does not add an artificial frame timer.
routes.custom_audio: Choose and identify a real expansion before adding audio code. The stock absence is a capability distinction, not an unfinished silent routine.
routes.references: Sinclair, ZX81 BASIC Programming: INPUT, arithmetic, FAST/SLOW and display-file memory; recorded 1 KiB ROM configuration.

routes.name: BBC Micro
routes.configuration: BBC Model B MOS 1.20/BASIC II, MODE 6
routes.input_contract: read_controls scans Q/A/O/P/Space through MOS OSBYTE 129. It returns controls bits 1/2/4/8/16 for up/down/left/right/action, without consuming the character buffer. A/X/Y/flags change; key_index is private scratch.
routes.audio_contract: The SOUND block is eight bytes: channel 17 flushes and uses channel 1, amplitude -15, pitch 100, duration 2. OSWORD 7 copies it into MOS audio state. Playback is asynchronous; call from main with MOS IRQ services intact. A/X/Y/flags change.
routes.custom_input: Change the key-number/mask tables together. Read once, then derive pressed/released before replacing previous.
routes.custom_audio: Change the SOUND block. Queuing versus flushing is a deliberate channel policy; copying the block gives the OS its own queued parameters.
routes.references: Acorn, BBC Microcomputer Advanced User Guide / Electron technical documentation: OSBYTE &81 negative INKEY and OSWORD &07 SOUND block; MOS IRQ ownership.

routes.name: Acorn Electron
routes.configuration: Electron MOS/BASIC, MODE 6
routes.input_contract: read_controls scans Q/A/O/P/Space through MOS OSBYTE 129. It returns controls bits 1/2/4/8/16 for up/down/left/right/action, without consuming the character buffer. A/X/Y/flags change; key_index is private scratch.
routes.audio_contract: The SOUND block is eight bytes: channel 17 flushes and uses channel 1, amplitude -15, pitch 100, duration 2. OSWORD 7 copies it into MOS audio state. Playback is asynchronous; call from main with MOS IRQ services intact. A/X/Y/flags change.
routes.custom_input: Change the key-number/mask tables together. Read once, then derive pressed/released before replacing previous.
routes.custom_audio: Change the SOUND block. Queuing versus flushing is a deliberate channel policy; copying the block gives the OS its own queued parameters.
routes.references: Acorn, BBC Microcomputer Advanced User Guide / Electron technical documentation: OSBYTE &81 negative INKEY and OSWORD &07 SOUND block; MOS IRQ ownership.
